clue.text: Due for repair, orgasmatron perhaps lacking final ecstasy, a rather improbable device

definitions.note: a plot device so contrived it strains belief

indicators.note: something sent for repair gets taken apart and put back together, so these letters are rearranged
the phrase takes away the closing letter of the device's name

parts.note: the orgasmatron of Woody Allen's film Sleeper is an example of a sex machine
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Something is due for repair: a pleasure contraption that has lost its final thrill, and a rather far-fetched gadget at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for repair' turns DUE into DEU. 'lacking final' drops the last E (ecstasy) from SEX MACHINE, leaving SEX MACHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names a contrived intervention that resolves a plot, a dramatist's convenient but unlikely device.

clue.text: Unrealistically planned paper on Brexit finally accepted by unionists

indicators.note: something accepted by a group is taken into it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

indicators.note: takes the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A newspaper's take on leaving the EU, unrealistically conceived, is finally endorsed by Northern Ireland's unionists.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP, Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party, propped up the UK government during the Brexit talks, hence the topical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fanciful and impractical, invented without regard to reality, is said to be conjured in the imagination.

clue.text: What steers at outset nibbled?

indicators.note: a bite taken from the start removes the opening letter

parts.note: a rudder is the blade that steers a boat

explanation.surface: A question about what young cattle suckled on at the start of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steers' looks like young bullocks, and that is the whole-clue reading too: a calf nibbles at its mother's teats. Read as wordplay, 'What steers' is a ship's rudder, bitten at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The bag of mammary glands on a cow is what a calf feeds from.

clue.text: Romans perhaps sleep uneasily with it

definitions.note: Paul's letter to the Romans is one book of the New Testament

indicators.note: an uneasy sleeper tosses and turns, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The ancient Romans, perhaps, slept badly with it on their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romans' reads as the people of Rome, but it is the Biblical book.
explanation.definitionFit: Romans is one of the New Testament letters, which Bible readers call by an older word meaning letter.

clue.text: Making great drink that can cause you to see double!

definitions.text: that can cause you to see double!

parts.note: to magnify is to make something larger
a glass is a drink, as in 'have a glass of wine'

explanation.surface: A potent drink that gives you double vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see double' suggests drunkenness, but the lens makes things look twice their size.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand lens enlarges whatever you look at, so objects can appear twice as big.

clue.text: Like e.g. bowl of unfinished ice cream, melting

indicators.note: melted ice cream loses its shape, so these letters are reshaped
an unfinished word lacks its closing letter

explanation.surface: A bowl of half-eaten ice cream, melting away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts ICE to IC; 'melting' rearranges IC plus CREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is often made of fired clay, so it is pottery-like in material.

clue.text: Perhaps with bat juvenile, a high place is what will help early life?

parts.note: a cricketer holding the bat is batting, or 'in'
a cub is a young animal
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A puzzling scene of a young bat in a lofty spot, asking what nurtures life in its first days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with bat' points to cricket, where the side batting is 'in'. A TOR is a rocky hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This apparatus keeps eggs warm or premature babies safe, supporting life in its earliest stage.

clue.text: A fabric of choice

parts.note: twill is a woven cloth with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: A material someone would pick above all others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of choice' looks like it describes the fabric, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as one pleases means doing it by preference, freely chosen.

clue.text: Likeness of Quasimodo at end of novel?

parts.note: Quasimodo dies at the close of Victor Hugo's novel
the hunchback of Notre-Dame was its bell-ringer

explanation.surface: A portrait of the Hunchback of Notre-Dame as he appears in the novel's final pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Quasimodo is both pieces' subject: he rings the bells, and he is dead when Hugo's book ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who looks exactly like someone else is a perfect double, an uncanny resemblance.

clue.text: Cries of murder announcing motive

definitions.note: a murder is the collective noun for crows

indicators.note: something announced is said out loud, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a cause is a motive or reason

explanation.surface: A detective names the motive behind a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'murder' reads as a crime, but a group of crows is called a murder.
explanation.definitionFit: The harsh calls a crow makes are its characteristic noise.

clue.text: Break at a time that's about right for biscuits

indicators.note: goes around the next piece, holding it inside
breaking the words up lets the letters be rearranged

explanation.surface: Pausing for a few almond cookies at what feels like the proper time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like a tea break, but it is the anagram signal on AT A TIME; 'about' wraps those letters round R.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small Italian almond macaroons, a type of crisp cookie.

clue.text: Phone that may be suspended

definitions.meaning: a hanging decoration of balanced shapes that moves in air currents

explanation.surface: A telephone that could be cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a portable phone and a hanging sculpture of balanced parts.

clue.text: Follow the money, to encapsulate Trump's essence

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a purse is a sum of money, as prize money in boxing

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the surname of the US president

explanation.surface: An investigator's motto: trace the cash flows to get to the heart of Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow the money' is a stock investigative phrase, but only 'Follow' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase or go after something is to track it.

clue.text: Celebrity directors getting right to 14

definitions.note: the right-hand side, as seen from aboard the craft of 14 across

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
a company's directors make up its board

explanation.surface: Famous company directors acquiring a sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the answer to 14 across: the term for the right side of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors use this word for the right-hand side of a ship facing forward.

clue.text: Craft outlines of campaign launch, with Remain backing holding

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it
backing means going in reverse, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to stay is to remain

indicators.note: the outline of a phrase is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Brexit-era political sketch: the shape of a campaign launch, with the Remain side lending its support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remain backing' reads as support from Remain voters, but it is STAY written backwards, holding C and H, the outer letters of 'campaign launch'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sailing boats, and craft is a general term for vessels.

clue.text: What's needed to keep one's hand in before fight? Coach may have it

parts.words: What's needed to keep one's hand in
parts.note: a glove is what keeps your hand inside it
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A boxer's trainer advises keeping in practice before the bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep one's hand in' means staying in practice, but here it is literal. 'Coach' looks like a trainer, but it is a car or bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle's dashboard compartment for small items; a coach (bus) may have one.

clue.text: Refuse to die

explanation.surface: Someone who will not give up living.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to decline something offered and, euphemistically, to perish.

clue.text: Despicables carrying rubbish in manbag?

indicators.note: one piece carries the other inside it

parts.note: scum are despicable people
rot is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Nasty types smuggling junk in a men's shoulder bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manbag' is a fashion accessory; the question mark signals the playful anatomical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin pouch holding the testes is, jokingly, the bag every man carries.

clue.text: Crack inside tree from the east producing shrub

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left
one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an elm is a tree
to have a crack at something is to try it

explanation.surface: A crack inside a tree, seen from its eastern side, producing a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' reverses everything built so far, since across entries normally read west to east.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen bush with fragrant white flowers, sacred to Venus.

clue.text: Runner soon knackered during one kilometre uphill

definitions.note: a ski is a runner over snow

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
in a down clue, going uphill means reading bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: knackered is British slang for worn out, so these letters are broken up

explanation.surface: A jogger soon exhausted during a one-kilometre hill climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uphill' reverses the unit pair, and 'knackered' (British slang for exhausted) scrambles the fodder that goes inside. 'Runner' looks like an athlete, but it is a single ski.
explanation.definitionFit: A single broad ski on which the rider stands with both feet; skis are runners on snow.

clue.text: Fantastic player brought on by way of breaking in

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the other

parts.note: a sub is a substitute brought onto the field
per means by way of, as in per post

explanation.surface: A brilliant substitute brought on breaks into the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words express high praise for something excellent.

clue.text: Wood to do job of sleeper once top's cut off

indicators.note: the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a sleeper's job is to slumber

explanation.surface: Timber for railway sleepers, once its top is sawn off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeper' suggests a railway sleeper of wood, but it is someone asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumber is timber sawn into planks, especially in North American usage.

clue.text: Dishevelled, given tie in case

indicators.note: messed-up letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scruffy man handed a tie just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like 'in case', but it is a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive is one of the grammatical cases of nouns.

clue.text: Beat it, flipping Commie

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over

parts.note: a Red is a communist

explanation.surface: An angry instruction to a communist to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat it' reads as a dismissal and 'flipping' as an expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat in the sense of exhausted, dead beat, worn out.

clue.text: Great match, yours truly taking the lead

indicators.note: the piece moves to the front

parts.note: a game is a match
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A splendid match, with the speaker going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: ME moves from the end of GAME to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for terrific or huge.

clue.text: Copy two letters from Croatian into Serbian erratically first time

indicators.note: the leading letter of the following word is taken
one piece goes inside the other
erratic means irregular, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the opening pair of letters of Croatian

explanation.surface: Copying a couple of Croatian letters into Serbian, carelessly, at the first attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: CR goes into RANSIBE, the anagram of SERBIAN; T, the first letter of 'time', goes at the front. Serbian can use both Latin and Cyrillic script.
explanation.definitionFit: To write out a text again in full is to reproduce it.

clue.text: Group savaged sexism and system for rating figure?

parts.note: a body is an organised group

indicators.note: savaged words are torn apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: An organisation attacked sexism and a scoring system for women's looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like a number, but it is a person's physique.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratio of weight to height squared measures how heavy someone is for their build.
